DILG BAGONG PIUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City wvm.dilq.gov.ph OPINION No. s. 26k 'MAY 19 2025 HON. MARIA LIBRADA FE M. REYNA, ET AL. Sangguniang Panlungsod Member Office of the Sangguniang Panlungsod Dagupan City Dear SP Members: This has reference to your letter dated January 16, 2025, requesting this Department's legal opinion on the issues surrounding the Sanggunian Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP). Culled from your letter are the following relevant factual antecedents: • The membership of the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of Dagupan comprises the Vice Mayor, ten (IO) elected SP members, and two (2) ex-officio members in the persons of the ABC President and SK [Federation President]. Thus, the total membership of the sanggunian is thirteen (13), and its voting membership is twelve (12). • Prior to the 5 November 2024 sanggunian regular session, the sanggunian was in receipt of a preventive suspension order of three (3) of the regular SP members. • With nine (9) SP members and the Presiding Officer present, the sanggunian proceeded with its regular session. • However, the five (5) SP members belonging to the minority bloc, in the same session, proceeded to, among others: a. Declare all the committee chairmanships vacant (reorganization of committees); b. Voting in new chairpersons for the various standing committees; c. Adopt a new set of IRPs; and d. Selection of minority councilor Michael Fernandez as "Floor Leader" Hence, the following issues, which we herein quoted in verbatim: I. Whether or not, under our existing laws, the minority vote shall have precedence over the majority vote; 2. Whether or not, despite a contrary majority vote of all members, the standing committees, as reorganized illegally by the minority, shall remain; "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

3. Whether or not, despite a contrary majority vote of all members, the selection of committee chairpersons by the minority shall remain despite not achieving at least a 2/3 vote in accordance with our Internal Rules; 4. Whether or not, despite a contrary majority of all members, the adoption of the new Internal Rules, which contravened the sanggunian's Internal Rules, shall remain; 5. Whether or not [SP member] Michael Fernandez, despite a no-confidence vote by a majority of all members of the sanggunian, shall remain as "Floor Leader"; 6. Should the Presiding Officer refuse to recognize a main motion that is in order, preventing its discussion and vote, what is the legal recourse of the majority of the members? 7. What is the available legal recourse or remedies (criminal, civil, or administrative) to the members of the sanggunian when the City Secretary: a. Refuses to enforce a majority vote b. Refuses to enforce the Internal of Procedure 8. What is the available legal recourse or remedies (criminal, civil, or administrative) to members of the sanggunian, when the Vice Mayor as Presiding Officer: a. b. c. d. e. f. Refuses to entertain a main motion that is in order; Refuses to allow discussion and vote on such main motion; Refuses to recognize the Internal Rules of Procedure as established by majority vote; Refuses to enforce the contents of such Internal Rules of Procedure and the generally accepted rules of parliamentary procedure; Refuses to comply with existing Supreme Court jurisprudence and DILG Memorandum Circulars and Opinions in the processing of legislation in the sanggunian; Refuses to recognize the valid and legal manifestations and motions of the majority. 9. What is the remedy when the presiding officer still refuses to yield to the majority vote and insists on his ruling, likewise the inaction of the secretary? At the outset, we take particular note that the foregoing issues ultimately hinge on the propriety or legality of the reorganization of the sanggunian chairmanships and the adoption of a new set of the sanggunian IRP. Accordingly, if the reorganization of the sanggunian committee chairmanships and the adoption of the new IRP are legally valid, then the ancillary issues put forth are either moot or irrelevant. Having said that, it is to be noted that this Department has, time and time again, opined that matters involving the sanggunian committee and its membership should be governed by its duly adopted IRP. To first address the validity of acts undertaken by the minority bloc raised by queries No. 1-5, the key issue is whether the actions (e.g., reorganization, adoption of new IRPs, Page 2 of 4

etc.) undertaken during the absence of the suspended members are legally valid despite the actions being led by what is traditionally considered a minority bloc. We emphasize that Section 15 of the SP's IRP requires a 2/3 vote of all members (excluding the Presiding Officer) for reorganization and a majority vote for amendments to the IRP. However, the Supreme Court in Aldovino v. COMELEC and Avelino v. Cuenca has clarified that members preventively suspended are not legally qualified to exercise their official functions, including voting and being counted in determining quorum or majority. Similarly, the Supreme Court in the case of Avelino v. Cuenca,l excluded a member of the Senate in the determination of quorum in the sessions of the Senate since the excluded Senator was in the United States and, therefore, outside the coercive jurisdiction of the Senate. In effect, this situation would effectively reduce, for the time being, the quorum of the Senate. By analogy, the preventive suspension order against the concerned sangguniang members constitutes a legal restriction for them to discharge their powers, duties, and functions. Accordingly, the preventive suspension of the 3 SP members had effectively reduced the number, for the time being, in determining the qualified majority vote required for the reorganization of the sanggunian committee chairmanships and the amendment of its IRP. Based on the facts and circumstances presented therefore, the total voting membership for purposes of that session was effectively reduced, and the computation for majority or 2/3 thresholds must be based only on the active, qualified members at that time. Accordingly, the reorganization of committee chairmanships, adoption of new IRPs, and designation of a floor leader were lawful—provided the required vote based on the reduced number was met. Further to this discussion is Query No. 6 which pertains to the legal recourse if the presiding officer refuses to recognize a proper motion. Under parliamentary procedure, when the Presiding Officer unjustifiably refuses to entertain a main motion that is in order, the majority of the body may raise a point of order and appeal the ruling of the chair. If the chair persists in refusal, the body may move to declare the chair's seat temporarily vacant (for the purpose of presiding) and proceed with the agenda through a designated acting presiding officer from among themselves. With regard queries No. 7-8, when the City Secretary or Vice Mayor fails to act in accordance with the Will of the majority or internal rules, the remedies against the inaction are as follows: a. Administrative Recourse: A verified complaint may be filed with the Office of the Ombudsman or the Civil Service Commission (for career service personnel) for neglect of duty, insubordination, or grave misconduct. 83 Phil. 17 Page 3 of 4

For the Vice Mayor, administrative charges under Section 60 of the LGC may be pursued for dereliction of duty, abuse of authority, or violation of rules. b. Judicial Recourse: The aggrieved majority may seek injunctive relief or mandamus from the proper courts to compel compliance with duly approved IRPs and lawful resolutions. c. Criminal Remedies: If bad faith, evident partiality, or corruption is involved, criminal liability under the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (RA 3019) may arise. Finally, query No. 9 pertains to persistent defiance by the Presiding Officer or the Secretary. If the Presiding Officer and City Secretary continue to disregard the lawful acts and majority decisions of the sanggunian, the following actions may be prudent: • The SP members may ask assistance from the DILG Regional Office for guidance in line with its exercise of general supervision or file administrative complaints with the Ombudsman, citing deliberate obstruction of legislative functions. • They may also elevate the matter to the courts for judicial affirmation of the legality of their acts, ensuring that legislative processes are not indefinitely paralyzed. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . ROMEO P. BENITEZ A Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Cc: JONATHAN PAUL M. LEUSEN, JR., CESO 111 Regional Director.
